question: An 8-month-old boy is brought to his pediatrician by his parents with a 12-hour history of fever and coughing. He has also been experiencing intermittent diarrhea and skin abscesses since birth. Otherwise, he has been meeting developmental milestones as expected. Analysis of this patient's sputum reveals acute angle branching fungi, and culture shows gram-positive cocci in clusters. A flow cytometry reduction test was obtained that confirmed the diagnosis. Which of the following processes is most likely defective in this patient?

options.ope: Transforming superoxide radicals into hydrogen peroxide

analysis: This patient's clinical presentation with recurrent skin abscesses, fever, cough, and diarrhea along with the presence of acute angle branching fungi in sputum and gram-positive cocci in clusters on culture suggests a diagnosis of chronic granulomatous disease (CGD). CGD is a primary immunodeficiency disorder characterized by defective phagocyte function, specifically the inability of phagocytes to generate reactive oxygen species (superoxide radicals) needed for microbial killing.
